title: Valid Palindrome
summary: You get a string `s`. Decide whether it reads the same forward and backward once you ignore letter case and drop every character that is not a letter or digit.

examples.explanation: Keeping letters and digits and lowercasing gives "racecar".

approaches.twist: Skip characters that are not letters or digits, and compare in lowercase.
Build a cleaned lowercase copy and compare it with its reverse.
approaches.note: Works, but uses O(n) extra space. The target is O(1).

signals.phrase: reads the same forward and backward

constraintReading: len(s) up to 2·10⁵ means O(n) or O(n log n). The O(1) space target rules out building a cleaned copy.

hints.clarify: Does a space count? Does 'A' equal 'a'? Try "No, on!" by hand: which characters matter?
hints.approach: Two pointers from both ends. Compare the characters they point at and move inward, skipping characters that do not count.
hints.whyNot: A hash map does not help: order matters here, not counts.

slots.setup: l at 0, r at the last index.
slots.update: Move l right past characters that do not count; move r left the same way.
slots.record: Compare the two characters in lowercase; if they differ, stop with False.
slots.return: If the loop finishes, return True.

solution.explanation: Each pointer moves inward at most n times, so the time is O(n). Only two integers are stored, so the space is O(1).

events.label: skip
events.say: s[{l}] is {s[l]!r}, not a letter or digit, so l moves right

events.label: skip
events.say: s[{r}] is {s[r]!r}, not a letter or digit, so r moves left

events.label: mismatch
events.say: They differ, so it is not a palindrome

events.label: return
events.say: The pointers met: every pair matched

related.relation: Also moves two indexes toward each other, but the middle decides which half to drop.
